name: Mental-health and therapy practices (admin)

problems.words: Late cancellations leave practitioners with empty hours
quick_ideas: Count late cancellations per practitioner for a week, so the loss is measured
Make sure every client has seen the cancellation policy, so it is clear.

workzap_build.text: online booking per practitioner with reminders and a policy acknowledgement at booking, tracking cancellations as they happen.

problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and policy flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which appointment hours stayed empty after late cancellations this week, so you can see where practitioner time is being lost.
Give one admin person the daily job of offering newly empty hours from one written standby list, so fewer cancellations leave gaps.

problems.words: We have a long waitlist but some practitioners still have gaps
quick_ideas: List waitlist requests by service type, language and availability, so matches are easier
Compare that with practitioners' open hours, so gaps can be offered.

workzap_build.text: a waitlist and matching board showing open requests and time on list, offering freed slots to matched clients.

problems.free_stops: Matching rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count waitlist requests that match each practitioner's usual hours and service type, so hidden fit problems stand out against the backlog.
Give one staff member a fixed time each day to match open hours with the waitlist notebook, so gaps get offered sooner.

problems.words: Intake forms come in on paper, email and WhatsApp
quick_ideas: Stop accepting intake details over WhatsApp, so sensitive information isn't scattered
Pick one secure route for forms, so admin checks one place.

workzap_build.text: workflow_automation — a digital intake form with secure submission and a completeness check for the admin role.

problems.free_stops: Form set-up and security are in the solution document; record-keeping rules are for your adviser.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many new intake forms arrived through each route this week, so you can see which channel creates the most chasing.
Give one staff role the job of logging every new form into one notebook on arrival, so admin stops checking scattered places.

problems.words: Associates argue about the fee split and room charges
quick_ideas: Put each associate's split and room charge on one signed page, so there is one reference
Share a monthly session count, so both sides agree the base.

workzap_build.text: an associate pay and room-rental statement from completed sessions.

problems.ask_first: Do associates rent rooms or work on a split?
problems.free_stops: Statement rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many associate sessions changed, cancelled or moved after booking this week, so fee-split arguments can be traced to admin changes.
Give one admin role the weekly job of writing each associate's room-use exceptions in one notebook, so charge disputes have one reference point.

problems.words: No-show fees are never actually charged
quick_ideas: List this month's no-shows with fee status, so the amount is known
Agree who decides on waivers, so it is consistent.

workzap_build.text: a no-show and late-cancellation log with fee status and waiver approvals.

problems.ask_first: Is the fee in your written policy now?
problems.free_stops: Fee rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count this week's no-shows by whether a fee decision was marked the same day or left open, so delays behind missed charges stand out.
Give one front-desk role the closing-time job of marking every no-show as charged, waived or pending in one notebook, so missed fees stop being overlooked.

problems.words: Online session links get sent to the wrong person
quick_ideas: Send links only from the practice account, so personal phones aren't used
Add a check of the contact before sending, so errors are caught.

workzap_build.text: a scheduler that sends session links only to the booked contact and logs every send.

problems.ask_first: Which tool do you use for online sessions?
problems.free_stops: Send rules are in the solution document; confidentiality duties are for your adviser.

extra_ideas.text: Note each time a session link had to be resent or corrected this week, so the scale of sending mistakes is clear.
Give one staff role the job of sending all session links during a fixed daily window, so contact checks happen the same way each time.

problems.words: Insurance receipts and corporate invoices are made by hand
quick_ideas: Time how long receipts take each week, so the cost is known
List corporate accounts with balances, so late payers stand out.

workzap_build.text: credit_ledger — a receipt and invoice generator with payment tracking and ageing.

problems.free_stops: Document format is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which hand-made receipt and invoice requests arrive in bunches during the week, so you can spot the busiest admin pinch point.
Give one admin role a fixed weekly hour to write all pending receipts and corporate invoices from one paper list, so requests stop scattering across the week.

problems.words: Enquiries sit in the inbox for days
quick_ideas: Check reply times on last week's enquiries, so the delay is measured
Name one person for daily replies, so each enquiry has an owner.

workzap_build.text: an enquiry inbox with response timers and source tracking, routing anything urgent to staff with an emergency-signpost message.

problems.ask_first: How do enquiries reach you now?
problems.free_stops: Routing rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the arrival day and reply day on recent enquiries, so you can see how long the inbox is sitting untouched.
Give one staff member a set time each workday to clear new enquiries from one written list, so replies stop waiting in the inbox.

problems.words: Practitioners' licence and supervision renewals aren't tracked
quick_ideas: List each practitioner's renewal dates by role, so expiries are visible
Set reminders for the nearest dates, so none slip.

workzap_build.text: a licence and supervision calendar with reminders by role.

problems.free_stops: Reminder schedule is in the solution document; requirements are for your regulator.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many practitioner renewals fall in the same upcoming month by role, so workload clashes can be seen before papers pile up.
Give one admin role the monthly job of checking one paper renewal list by role, so upcoming licence and supervision dates stop being missed.

never_say: Any therapy, counselling, diagnosis, crisis or medication advice, including "what staff should say".
Anything about a client's situation, even in general terms.
Interpretations of confidentiality or record-keeping law.
Help sharing records without consent or issuing letters without proper sessions.
Ideas that record client names, reasons for seeking help or session content.
If anyone mentions suicide, self-harm or danger: emergency services first (and 9-8-8 in Canada).

sample_reply.person: Late cancellations are killing us. Therapists lose hours every week and we never charge the fee. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there is a way through this, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, count late cancellations per therapist for a week, so the lost time is measured.
Second, make sure every client has seen the cancellation policy, so it is clear before it is needed.
The next step up would be: with online booking, reminders, policy acknowledgement and a log of fees due.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
